reviews.review:
Best professor at UMD. He is funny, nice and presents the material in interesting ways.

However, this is not an easy class. It requires a lot of work, but it is definitely worth taking. I had never taken a psyc class before, and I was pleasantly surprised.

Take this class with Roberts if you can! Highly recommend.

Dr. Roberts is amazing! I had him in the fall, and I learned so much. It does require a substantial amount of time and work, but not at all unbearable. With that said, it is DEFINITELY worth it, because his style of teaching and assigning work it extremely beneficial; I learned A LOT, and i still remember a great deal of it five months later! He is a psychologist, so he knows the best way for us to learn, and applies it. Dr. Roberts makes Psych FUN and INTERESTING!

I had scott roberts this year for Psyc 100, and it was a lot of work.  That being said, it was extremely interesting.
Most of the work was done on weekends, with a "study guide" to be completed by the beginning of every week. the study guides took a long time at least 4 hours all put together, but he makes  the chapters himself and they are filled with videos and other things that make it a lot less boring than if he just gave us a textbook and told us to read.  If you study and do the work, though tiring at times, you will do fine.

Terrible professor. His quizzes are completely unfair. He says that his quizzes are strictly for him to tell if you're doing the reading and he said the answers can be found DIRECTLY from the readings. The problem is that half of the answers don't come from the reading...and you have to guess....which isn't fair because it's not in the reading... and he is NOT responsive to emails at all so if you try to explain why a question wasn't fair, he doesn't respond back (not professional...).  For the essays, the grading scheme is: A (100%), B- (82%)...you can't score anywhere between 100% and 82%..... like what??..So one content mistake or one grammar mistake will already drop you down to a B-....another mistake will drop you down to a C-. Therefore it's possible to fail every single essay. Not a fair professor at all.  Honestly, I'm a senior neurobio major so I've had some pretty tough/hard/unfair profs (like for Orgo2, Mam Phys, BCHM)...but honestly, curtis is the worst prof i've ever had here at umd.

Dr. Curtis is very knowledgable and a great lecturer. The class is a lot of work and some questions on the test are tricky, but if you put in the effort and complete all assignments you should easily get an A or B. There are clicker points each lecture so it's best to go to those. There's also MANY extra credit opportunities.

Good lecturer, but this class is A LOT of work.  You can not slack off.  The every other week Blended Learning Assignments were graded hard: you can only get a A, C, D, F and you can not redo them.  Discussion was a joke. Weekly 50 questions that are submitted on elems on Mondays and no redo.  The book is online(he wrote the book) so make sure you read everything. Test are HARD.  Good luck in the class!

NEVER TAKE PSYCH!!!

If you like clicker classes, tedious online weekly quizzes (which you will end up taking shortcuts on), obnoxious blended learning assignments, and pointless discussion (which you will skip)..... then take this class. Otherwise, if you're normal and don't want to pull your hair out, avoid it. NOTE: I'm not saying it is hard, it is just miserable. 

Now on Professor Curtis:

He's honestly one of the better teachers I had freshman year. He does a great job being prepared for class, he uses a variety of methods to convey the information, and he honestly loves the subject. I'm sure psych majors consider him incredible because he truly knows and loves his material. But, for the average Gen-ed satisfying student, he's just a pretty good teacher. 

He is very clear about his expectations and will not budge for almost anything. Read and follow the syllabus, and you won't ever need to even speak to him. Also, he is very available to the students and makes it clear that he is available to help with anything class-related. 

He's pretty funny, and even funnier when he gets pissed off about phones going off in class. (organize it one day to see; 4 rings going off should do the trick).

Overall, nobody can claim he's a jerk or unreasonable. He's strict, honest, and professional. The comments about him being condescending are slightly true, but for the most part that's just people being knit picky .

I had Curtis for PSYC100. He was very knowledgeable of anything to do with psychology and the way he led class and taught the material made sure that I was able to retain and apply everything that we learned. While he was strict on deadlines and assignments, he was willing to do what he could to make sure you succeed. I would recommend for any psychology class.

Really nice guy but i had a hard time with this class. Easy material but asks for a lot on tests. There was a lot of extra credit in the class especially toward the end. But the weekly blended learning assignments were graded very . poorly- you either got a A, C, or D which is unfair to me doesn't let you redo them either. overall this class has been annoying but it could definitely be worse.

Curtis as absolutely fabulous. Very funny in lecture and explains things clearly. He is accessible outside of class and is willing to clarify/answer if you have questions about subject matter. The only hard thing about the class is its size (PSYC 100). Grades don't tend to be posted on time, and the worksheets are real point-drainers/GPA killers. Wording in exams/worksheets is also not always completely clear. Curtis is a great lecturer, but the class itself doesn't measure up.
He claims to be on the students side, but in reality has 0 consideration for them.

Great guy! Dr. Curtis really knows his stuff and is very helpful in office hours if you're struggling with a concept. People really hate the class because they think it's a weed out course, but you'll do fine if you just do the work. The weekly worksheets are long and a pain, but all the answers are in the reading and help you study while you read. They can also be found online easily. There are 6 writing assignments, but again just answer the questions directly and without fluff and you'll be fine. Plus you can go to any of the TA office hours and they'll read over your papers before you turn them in. The exams can get you because they're multiple choice so you either know it or you don't but if you do all the work assigned it generally helps you study. Not a lot of extra credit.
She is awesome! I loved having her as a professor. She had us do a lot of hands-on activities to make sure we were engaged and paying attention.

Honestly one of the best teachers I’ve ever had. He explain concepts very well, make class fun by doing activities that help us understand and remember different concepts, and cracking a few jokes. He genuinely wants his students to learn the material. His tests are tricky, but if you study really hard, go to his office hours, and get good homework/quiz/attendance scores, you should do fine. I’d expect A- if you work really hard  but it’s so worth it because he’s a great teacher.

You can tell Selterman knows what he's talking about when he teaching during lecture. His exams are application based and are very tricky. However, exams are weighted less than the worksheets that we have to do every week, which take about 3 hours to do. I would do as well as possible on those quizzes, so the exam grades won't affect you as much. The class is interesting, but the workload kind of ruins it. It's not an easy A type class.

EASILY my favorite professor of all of freshman year! He very clearly loves teaching & psychology and has never had a boring lecture. I took PSYC100 and it was definitely on the easy side because he makes it a personal mission to make sure everyone in the class is doing well. He was also super accommodating with the online classes, and he's one of the reasons I'm now a psych major. take his class!! you will NOT regret it.
great professor and very nice. answers emails super fast and cares for his students!

Was a lot of work and I felt like it should honestly be a 4-credit class. While the content wasn't difficult, the workload felt overwhelming at times. Between weekly 30-50 question quizzes, and having essays due every other week, it was rough for me. Don't take this class unless required.
The nicest and most understanding professor during this pandemic. Please take his class he genuinely wants you to learn! He made us do projects instead of exams and made the final one optional!

Dr. Jones was a solid teacher. Although my course was 100% asynchronous I could still gather that he was knowledgeable about the topics and passionate about helping students succeed. The textbook for this course was amazing (and free). Dr. Jones gave lots of interesting assignments and was extremely consistent in the amount of work he required each week. I do wish we had more ways to incorporate more interaction with other students, but I understand the course was all online and asynchronous which made it difficult.

Very good professor and he is obviously very aware of what's going on with the pandemic and how to ensure that his students can hold open discussions about what is going on in the world. He gives a lot of extra credit assignments. As long as you do your work on time and complete extra credit assignments, you should get an A in this class. He is a bit egotistical about some philosophies as others have mentioned but overall, he is a very well-spoken professor. The same goes for his TAs
Definitely a 10/10 professor. His lectures were super fun and engaging, and the assignments he gave each week helped solidify the material we had to learn. Definitely a professor I reccomend

Is he good at actually teaching? Absolutely! Am I coming out of this semester knowing more about psychology than I did? Yep! Is there a heavy workload? Yes to that too. However, unfortunately he is very quick to report students to the OSC over minor similarities found using turnitin.com, as helpful as this website can be, it can't be too heavily relied on for student work, especially when the professor specifically states that proper APA format and references aren't required for these 400-500 word essays, not just that, neither him nor my TA contacted me beforehand to clarify the situation. I'm sure he's great in an offline setting, but online, he jumps to conclusions and has power trips if you bring up how harshly a TA may grade your papers. I will also be taking his PSYC234 class next semester when we're fully back on campus so hopefully I'll have a better review.

IF YOU HAVE THE OPTION TO TAKE HIM, DO IT! One of the best professors I have had so far. Very organized and makes lectures and topics super easy to follow. There are 7 essay but he is a pretty chill grader and in smaller classes he will given opportunities for feedback before grading the paper. He does not put in 0 for late assignment unless you do not do anything. One of the best natural science classes to take! He does exam reviews and gives out candy!

Definitely the kindest professor ever, so glad that I had the opportunity to take his class. He teaches virtually from Florida but makes online learning so fun and easy to follow/understand. He's a very fair grader and very understanding. He has a rule that if something is due at 11:59, he won't count it as late as long as you hand it in before 10 AM the next day (and even then he doesn't take off many points for late assignments). He also starts every lecture by asking each student how they are and if they have anything fun that they want to share with the class which shows that he actually cares about his students and wants to connect with them.

I think professor Selterman is a solid professor overall. The course work is extremely manageable (a worksheet once a week and a 500-word short response once every other week.) He also doesn't require you to come to class in person and offers both an in-person as well as zoom option which is very convenient. The grading is pretty fair on the short responses as it's mostly the TA's grading them. He's very ingrained in his beliefs which can make it a bit hard to have a meaningful discussion if you disagree with him or present a counterargument to his point of view. But it's nothing ridiculous like I've seen in some of these reviews. No exams are a huge plus too. I would take him again for sure and I enjoyed how manageable the workload is

I put it in very minimal effort in this class and got an A. It was so easy. The professor doesn’t have any exams. You have an open note worksheet quiz every week, and a paper every other week. The TA’s do all the grading and they usually go pretty light. I also did not learn anything and could not help anybody with this class, but at least it was a GPA boost.

Both the professor and the TA for this class are very nice. Exams are heavily weighted though!!
 If you have a strong passion for psychology I would definitely recommend taking her class.

Very easy A, just do the weekly worksheets and short SAs. Try to do the Clicker questions because it doesn't matter if you get them wrong as long as you participate. Dylan is nice and sometimes funny but he goes off topic. He let you choose in-person and zoom, there are no exams or final projects, and the course load is fair. It's a great elective to boost your GPA and the content is very interesting.

i only went to two lectures and still got an a. jones is pretty convenient bc you can watch lectures on elms. you don't need to buy a textbook. his recorded lectures were always great. great for intro to psyc!

Very easy class, but her lectures do not cover anything about the exams and oftentimes even the chapters. If you want to take a class about racism take this class. I often was scared to challenge her because I am a white male and was afraid she would tell me I am using my privilege over her. When teachers begin to suppress people's ideas and not have an open mind, this becomes dangerous.

Such a chill and understanding professor. Clearly knows her stuff, which makes lectures easy to follow along with. The workload isn't anything to blow off, but I highly recommend you take her class if you genuinely want to learn about psychology.

Professor Parham is so nice and the class is not difficult at all. Just go to his exam reviews where he goes over the entire test and take notes and you should be able to ace the test no problem. I wish I could take him for more classes.

Dr. Jones lectures very well, and it is very convenient that you can watch the lectures online. My only complaint is the amount of work. Every week, you have about 6 hours of homework from this class alone. He does not provide extensions nor does he reply to your emails about feeling overwhelmed with work.

I received an 104% in this class due to extra credit he offered and the class being extremely easy, this class was one of the easiest A's I've ever gotten, he offers no midterms, no finals. All you have to do is do the worksheets, and put effort into the SAs due every other week. I got 30/30 on almost every SA assignment except one time I got a 27/30 because I was lazy and just typed something out quickly. I would recommend him if you just want a chill, easy class. I also enjoyed the conversations he would have with the class. We barely went over actual content but it was interesting to engage in current topics in psychology like social media, the American education system, etc. Some people didn't like this but I actually enjoyed this a lot, it was the only reason I came to class. I think Selterman is a great professor.

Dr. Jones is great!  he is young which is nice because he gets or sense of humor and the class as a whole is pretty chill!  People are complaining about the work but it's one quiz on elms each week that you have an entire week to do, it's untimed, and you can open and close it as many times as you want.  Exams were online even though the class was in person which was nice!  He makes the content interesting and even lets you earn extra points after exams as a chance to kind of "redo it".  Hihgly recommend Dr. Jones, he's great!

Class was relatively boring, almost no one showed up. It wasn't too bad, it was more of a lack of participation that made it boring. She had "attendance" grades but those are just clickers and can be done at home. However, this class is very easy; lots of extra credit opportunities and huge test curves. She also allowed full pages for notes on the test, you could basically fit the entire chapter's material on it. There are also a total of 5 "essays", they are only 500 words and pretty straightforward. If you follow the rubric and make it comprehensive, you will get most of the points. The only real con is that you learn mostly from the homework worksheets that she gives, but they're easy. I would say that she knows what she is talking about and enjoys teaching the material, though. I would recommend this class as it's not too much of a workload.

I can tell that Dr.Vandaalen is sweet but she is not meant to be a professor. Lectures were the biggest waste of time and the tests were impossible. We were always graded harshly and feedback was limited so we were always unsure of how to improve. The only saving grace was the huge curve and extra credit. Don't take her if you don't have to!

I really enjoyed her class. Exams were relatively easy, if you knew how to answer the questions from the study guide you were guaranteed an A on the exam. Dr.Vandaalen is a very nice and understanding professor, she provided numerous opportunities for extra credit so make sure you take advantage of that

PROS: very nice and caring professor, allows for lots of extra credit opportunities, allows for a full 8x11 front and back cheat sheet, and gives a generous curve on exams, 5 easy papers IF you follow the rubric

CONS: exams were excessively difficult(class average was never above 65% for any of the 3 exams), even when I felt as though I had a good understanding of the content questions revolved around tricky little details from the class rather than knowledge of the overall concept, this was annoying, and if it weren't for the curve this class would've been way more stressful. Almost all the learning comes from the homeworks which aren't bad but a bit tedious. She also wasn't a great lecturer, seemed new and nervous, sometimes I honestly felt like I could answer questions and explain the answer more clearly than she would. Overall, be thankful for the curve.

The lectures were so boring and honestly useless because no one showed up and she made it discussion based. Participation is graded on clicker questions that can be done at home which was nice. The textbook (Open Psyc) was such a bore to read at times, but you only need to read it in preparation for the exams for which we were allowed a 8x11 sheet of paper to put notes on. Discussion section was extremely useless but it's only every other week so it wasn't too bad. She curves heavily and gives lots of extra credit. The class itself is easy to pass, but you won't be learning anything in this class. If you're interested in the subject, take this class with a different professor. Otherwise, it's a chill class.

Nothing bad to say about Dr. Vandaalen. She makes this class very easy and managable. Grades are pretty simple, with participation clicker questions, weekly HW, exams, and writing assignments. She really wants you to succeed and will allow for lots of EC opportunity and curves very generously. By far one of my best teachers during the semester.

The lecture content is interesting and he's a good lecturer - definitely a character to listen to. Lecture is not mandatory, discussion sections are. Textbook is free and accessible online. If you don't plan accordingly, his assignments can be overwhelming and difficult because they are due in the middle of the week at 4pm (usually). They will be difficult to do well on if you don't read so don't think you can get away with a good grade by not doing the required weekly readings. The readings are time consuming as well but I found them pretty interesting so it wasn't too bad. Discussion sections are mandatory and they grade you on your attendance/participation. Honestly, the discussion section was the worst part of this class because the activities weren't helpful or relevant, just busy work. It would've been nice if they had reiterated content/ideas learned in lecture but nope, they fed you an entirely different topic irrelevant to lecture. Aside from that, it's a good class. You will be REQUIRED to volunteer for research studies for a total of three credits, most of which you can do online. Just make sure to knock them out earlier on because you have to do them on your own time and they are annoying to do. Great class, highly recommend professor Jones.

Quite literally one of the greatest teachers at UMD, not only as a teacher but as a person as well. Professor Parham is very understanding and is there to help you succeed. He helps you understand psychology to a level you can apply it to your daily life, rather than just feed you information. Every assignment was with a purpose, and they were all very engaging. The Scientific Analysis, was definitely the hardest part of this class, but if you work on them in advance you should be fine. Exams were straightforward and easy. This guy is a GOAT. Take him if you see him. Best of luck.
-

Dr.Vandaalen is a really great professor, she makes the class easy, and she is always available when you are in need of help both in person and via email. The exams all have a curve which is really great, and there are a ton of options for extra credit opportunities in case anyone does need it. In general she makes psychology really interesting and fun to learn. By far one of my most favorite professors I've ever had at this university
Amazing guy, had fun and learned so much. Some papers and exams/quizzes, but all manageable

Professor Vandaalen is very nice and very caring. However, her class is incredibly boring and barely covers any of the information in the textbook. Going to the lectures was a complete waste of time and I didn't get much out of them. I would have preferred actually learning a lot of the information that was in the textbook as opposed to learning about one small thing in the chapter. The tests were impossible and were incredibly difficult. I only did well because the curve was insane. Every test the curve would add at least 20 points. That said, I will say that Professor Vandaalen wants her students to do well and that is why she offers a bunch of extra credit assignments and curves the tests a ton. I am so appreciative that she was kind enough to do this. However, I would recommend taking the other Professor for PSYC100 such as Jones because my friends had him and did absolutely no work and their tests were open book and online as opposed to our tests being in person on a scantron and we were only allowed one doubled-sided piece of paper. In closing, Vandaalen is a very nice and caring person but I wouldn't go through all the hard work and stress to get the grade you want. Just take the easy A with the other professor.

The 5-star reviews are not overexaggerating. As a senior, Professor Parham is one of the instructors who left a significant impact on my career. Not only is he understanding and accommodating to life circumstances, he also genuinely cares about the progress of his students. Taking psyc100 with him reinforced my interest in the field and 4 years later I am just as motivated to learn more about psychology as I was when taking the intro course with Professor Parham. If you have the option to take a class with him, do it!

I took him in Spring 2022. He's a good lecturer and tries to make the content interesting. Aside from the PowerPoints, he also includes visuals (mainly videos) to accompany the information. The workload of the course was extremely heavy for a 100-level class in my opinion, but I think that's uniform throughout all sections regardless of professor. Lectures weren't mandatory, but he did have clicker assignments during lecture that were graded for participation. The discussions were mandatory and they take attendance each time, and they happen every other week. There's an online textbook that's provided for all students. There were 3 take-home exams (including the final) when I had him, application activities every other week (the week's that you didn't have discussion), worksheets (which are like quizzes on ELMS) for each module, and learning activities. He also had exam reflections to try to gain back some points on exams. I would grade the general course worse, but Dr. Jones makes it bearable for the most part.

This class is overall very easy, you have reading quizzes that are online, easy papers that as long as you reach the page limit you should get a 100%, and three exams that are open book and open note that you take online. But the lectures are a waste of time honestly, you learn more from the book than you do from listening to her because she would talk about politics a lot. And as someone who doesn't share her views, I would just stay silent. But she is a very nice teacher and is very fair and reasonable (you don't even have strict due dates) and it was nice hearing her personal stories sometimes but the content just turned into a political tangent and some of the writing is very political.

She grades very easily, but some of her lectures seem off topic. The exams are all online and open note which is amazing. It is important to attend the lectures because she includes stuff from class on her exams, and she offers the answers to extra credit assignments.

Great engaging professor. She lectures like she's a stand up comedian. Midterms and final exams are online and open note. Lecture slides posted to ELMS which is helpful. Many opportunities for extra credit. Would take another class with her; she's passionate about PSYC for sure!

She was wonderful. Offers a lot of opportunities for extra credit which is great. Her lectures were always fun and you could tell she tries really hard to make them engaging. Would definitely recommend to anyone

I think that Professor Parham was great. I took an online class with him and he was very caring and a nice professor. His lectures were interesting and I was often engaged. He takes late work but of course try to get everything in on time if you can so it does not overwhelm you at the end.
Great professor and an extremely easy class. She accepted late work with no points off. She explained the content well and always knew the answers to student questions.

I would not recommend prof Vandaalen for PSYC100. Lectures are extremely boring with and basically useless for learning the material and doing well on the exams. Exams are very hard, making your notes extremely important for success on the exams. It really seems like lectures barely cover any of the required material for exams. If it weren't for extra credit opportunities and curves on exams, this class would be very hard. I know other teachers are way more chill and require much less work than her. She's a nice person that is accommodating, but I found myself doing way more work than expected. Especially when compiling good notes before exams. You will not learn much in this class.

Dr. Jones is a good lecturer, and his classes are very interesting and engaging. You will likely enjoy this class. Some of the application activities are difficult (particularly the ones were you are required to read actual psychology studies), but overall I enjoyed the class quite a bit. The exams are super easy and open note.
Good lecturer and makes lectures informative and entertaining. Exams are online and open note which is nice. Discussions are biweekly and mandatory. Overall great teacher and a good class.

Great professor, he genuinely wants to teach and help students and his lectures are quite interesting and somewhat interactive. He is overall a great person with an open mind and awareness. If you want an intro to psychology, then definitely take this because even if you don't pursue psychology later, this course will help you out in your life later on.

Professor Parham is easily one of the best professors I have had. He is engaging and truly cares about his students in an impactful way. Super interesting lectures, exams are straight forward, and essays are relevant and simple as long as you do what is asked. Highly recommend.

She was a really good psyc100 professor. Class was not too hard and she is very engaging in lectures. Very passionate about the subject and she was approachable about any questions about the course or psychology in general.

Professor Nicholas is a legend! She has such an incredible personality and makes lecture interesting and exciting. She is very excited to teach and loves her students. The class is not too bad. There is a quiz every week based on the readings which aren't too hard and there are 3 exams which are open note and online which are pretty easy. I recommend taking this class with Nicolas because she really is an amazing person and wants all of her students to do well.

Had her for Fall 2022, wouldn't recommend over other teachers for this class. It never felt like a gened and required more work than necessary. You're going to spend a lot of time compiling notes for the open-note exams, but the notes still didn't help sometimes because the exams were very difficult. Thank god she curves them, otherwise nobody would get an A. Classes are terribly boring and most of it is just review from what you had to learn for the online quizzes every Monday. Wednesdays were completely useless because they're taught by TA's (who were very nice, but they didn't give anybody any new information). You have to do an essay every two weeks, and that's not so bad. You can also complete every quiz and essay online weeks in advance if you put in the effort, which is nice. Basically, if you're good with notetaking and have a lot of time on your hands, this class is for you.

Professor Jones is entertaining and endearing, he may ramble a bit in his lectures but they are generally fun to listen to. There are a lot of assignments throughout each week, but they are generally not difficult and not too time-consuming. Very laid back and fun intro course!

This is the worst class if you are trying to fill a prerequisite and never want to do anything with psychology. His lectures are long and a waste of time, briefly covering contend and then showing you multiple youtube videos. One lecture was spent almost entirely on the blue/black vs white/gold dress and spun it as "perspective." I find him to be unprofessional, seemingly unqualified as a professor, and truly got nothing out of his class except for the passionate distain for psyc100. On top of his unprofessionalism, his assignments for class are worse than busy work you did in high school and a complete waste of time, then graded harsher than they should for a 100 level class that is the biggest joke. Not an easy A and if you are a busy stem major do not waste your time with this joke of a class or professor.

joke of a professor and joke of a class. Complete waste of time and worse than high school busy work. the only thing i learned is i hate psyc100 and i wasted my time and money just so i could take a prerequisite.

this class was such a mess. my psyc section was completely on zoom, so dr. abi would constantly get distracted and wouldn't stay on track. perhaps her in person classes are better, but don't take her online

The reviews are true. Any review of fewer than 5 stars is truly from someone who put no effort into the course.
Professor Parham is a professor who truly cares about his students and what he teaches. He tells stories, shows videos, and makes the class interactive even through Zoom. He is a person who really understands college students and how we act. His essays ARE moderately challenging, so starting them a day before will get you ready and a good grade, but that's out of his control. 
If you get to know him more, he's a really cool guy in general. He's a compassionate guy who will understand if you have trouble, as he really wants to connect with his students. 
Highly recommend! Get into his class! Don't get any other professor! I kid you not you will not regret it.
Honestly not a bad class. The quizzes can sometimes be annoying but he is a very dedicated professor and really knows what he is talking about

I took this class completely online and had a great experience. She was a kind teacher who was interesting to listen to. The format of the class was easy to follow and the weekly assignments were super easy. The exams were a bit difficult, but not impossible and very fair. The class was not time consuming at all, but I was still able to learn a bit. Definitely recommend, especially for online.
Tons of extra credit, easiest A of my life highly reccomend!

He's nice and all but I found his lectures pointless to go to. It takes less than 20 minutes to read his lecture slides for the 80 minute class. I was disappointed with this class though, mainly because my TA was a horrific grader, and I got a B in the class when I could've easily gotten a A had it not been for my TA.

Dr. Vandaalen was one of the kindest professors I've had. However, the class structure was kind of confusing. The course consisted of a lecture and review session each week with clicker questions, readings, a worksheet due each week before class and writing assignment due every two weeks, and the midterms/final. The class is set up into small circles/groups with a TA at each group to lead the discussion. I found the lectures to be very engaging and taught us how the course content could be applied to our daily lives. The content does not come from a traditional textbook, but rather a free resource that teaches through articles and videos. While she provided resources so we knew what to expect for the exams, there were a lot of very specific and random details from the videos or articles being tested that I felt more so assessed our ability to memorize small facts rather than our knowledge of psychology. That being said, it's very easy to get an A in this class as Dr. Vandaalen provides an insane amount of extra credit opportunities and curves. It's definitely more work than some of the other geneds I've taken, but I would recommend taking her for PSYC100!

do not take professor jones. he does not teach during lectures and his tests don't even cover the material we learn in class. i swear he pulls it out of thin air. he must be writing these reviews himself bc he's not this good.

Dr. Abi is such a good professor. She is very clear in her lectures and uses real world examples to further understanding of topics. She engages the class really well and is very relatable/ talking to you as though you are her friend during her lecture. Her exams are all online but you need to make sure you actually do the readings. If you do the readings/submit things on time/ and just show up for participation credit,You’ll get an A.

Definitely would recommend for PSYC100. She makes the lectures interesting and enjoyable and has a good sense of humor. Exams are all online and open note, and there are only three of them that make up 10% of your grade each, all multiple choice. Be sure to read the textbook section for each week and take decent notes from both the textbook and lecture, as you won't have time to find all of the information on the exams if you don't know anything. The other 70% of your grade essentially comes from showing up to discussion, doing the worksheets (basically online mini-quizzes with no time limit), syllabus quizzes and exam reflections. She gives easy extra credit opportunities as well. As long as you do the assignments and go to discussion, you're pretty much guaranteed a good grade.
Nice professor. Exams are open note and were curved a good amount.
Awesome guy. super understanding especially revolving around campus issues. Lectures are hard to learn from but if you do the readings you will be fine. Love him

Honestly, this class is really easy to get an A with the assignments she assigns to us. The only assignments you turn in are chapter reflections, which are pretty straightforward, plus chapter reading quizzes which should be simple to do as well. There will also be mini exams after a couple chapters, but luckily they're online, which is the benefit. She is a very kind person and she shows dedication in her teaching. She explains her lectures really well and they are easy to understand, a lot of the notes I would write down are based on what she says rather than what would be on the lecture slides so that shows how interesting her explanations are. She tries to use up her time with digesting each chapter and I believe it is worth learning and gaining from from this professor, would recommend her. Besides easily passing her class, but also learning things from her.

Lovely professer, very nice and empathetic teacher who was very understanding with assignments. I liked how she uses her clients experiences to relate to class chapters. Would take again! :) Exams are online and you can take them anywhere, as well as the quizzes (super easy, answers are directly in the chapters).

Loved Professor Barnet. He was super funny, and personable. Something especially helpful was his explanation of the applications of concepts that could be confusing. He made Psych extra interesting, which persuaded me to take his social psych class, PSYC221. The only thing that I wasn't a huge fan of was how fast he would go through slides and would have to skip sections of content due to timing. Overall, he is a great professor and I recommend taking any of his psych classes.
This actually might be the best professor I've ever had in my life. He's a great professor and seems to genuinely want everyone to succeed in the course.

This class is certainly a 100 level which meant I did find the lectures pretty easy and found myself losing points more because of sentence counts and such than actual incorrect information but Dr. Jones does a really good job lecturing and teaching. He's a super charming guy and clearly cares for and understands his students with grade policies to match. We got 2 of our weekly quizzes dropped and only had to attend discussion every other week which meant this course is very manageable. Would certainly recommend especially if just needing to get the psyc100 credit done

Hi so I was told that this class was super easy and took little effort because all the tests were online. They ARE online, but a lot of other stuff goes into your grade and I wasn't expecting that so I fell behind early in the semester. It's not a super strenuous class, but don't expect it to be *easy*. Dr. Nicolas was pretty nice, but it was a huge lecture hall so I never really got to know her at all.

Dr. Parham is by far the best professor I've had at UMD. I was contemplating taking psych100 for one of my GenEds since I had heard mixed opinions about the course, but saw Parham had an open spot in his lecture so I decided to try it out. This has been my favorite class, but I think it was all due to Parham and his teaching style. His lectures were interesting and straight forward, and he made great personal connections and shared stories so that students were able to memorize the concepts. As long as you do the homeworks (which take less than 30 minutes each week) and watch the lectures you are set to get a good grade on the exams. You will not regret taking this professor!

Dr. Barnet is the undisputed GOAT. He makes psychology more interesting than it is which is already hard to do with his engaging lectures and authentic personality. He's super funny, down to earth, and always looking to strike up conversations with students. He's also super young so he understands the youth and how we learn best. His workload is super doable and interesting. He dropped one of our tests as well, as long as you study you should be golden for them although the final was a bit harder than his usual exams. Overall 100% recommendation.
The reviews arent lying. Please take PSYC with him. Hes literally the goat and the class is easy if you put in any ounce of effort
Definitely recommend. Her lectures are interesting, her grading is fair, and her exams are all open-note, online, and based on the info received.

Dr. Barnet is the undisputed GOAT. He makes psychology more interesting than it is which is already hard to do with his engaging lectures and authentic personality. He's super funny, down to earth, and always looking to strike up conversations with students. He's also super young so he understands the youth and how we learn best. His workload is super doable and interesting. He dropped one of our tests as well, as long as you study you should be golden for them although the final was a bit harder than his usual exams. Overall 100% recommendation.

Dr. Abi is an amazing professor!! I took her online/in person section and it was very manageable and she is very organized with PSYC100. Quizzes and exams are from the textbook, and the discussions every other week are easy and informative. Participation is required if you want to get those clicker points, and Dr. Abi offers many extra credit opportunities. She is genuinely passionate about psych and her lectures were never boring. As long as you take good notes for the quizzes and exams, go to discussions and lectures, you’ll get an A!

Dr. Nicolas seems nice, and isn't a dry lecturer, but this class is still very boring. Very easy A, but there are mandatory discussions + posts + worksheets + stuff that can bring down your grade if you aren't careful to be very on top of things. Her exams are online, which is convenient. I have no strong opinions about her just was bored out of my mind every class and got an A without trying, so if you're just trying to pass this class as a requirement for your major I see no reason not to have her as your prof.
Chill guy, down to earth, likes to relate to the students.

The professor is great. She's super nice and a funny lecturer. However I feel like the workload was a bit much. Every week there were chapter notes to do. While this wasn't required, I found that you needed to complete it in order to do well and pass the exams. The exams are online but they can be very nit-picky and ask questions about some random video watched in lecture. Overall, the class is easy but you definitely need to put good work in.

Class was easy but super boring, you have to attend lectures for the clickers but the exams weren't anything too crazy. Only downside for me was my TA was a harsh grader and took off points for miniscule things.

Professor Parham is great. I’m sad I only had him for a winter semester, as it was online as well. He loves teaching PSYC100, and it clearly shows. His lectures are the opposite of boring, and they’re really fun to participate in. The work is very easy, and grading isn’t that harsh. As long as you try at least a little you’ll get an A.

If you want an easy A, TAKE THIS CLASS. I stopped going to lectures because they were boring/long, but I got As on my exams because I did all the required readings. Dr. Nicolas is very nice and engages with the class. I had a good TA, so my discussions weren't bad, and they were on Zoom. Exams are open note, but sometimes, she asks very niche questions that could only be answered if you went to the lecture. A lot of people are complaining about there being a "heavy workload," but it was literally like 2 assignments a week that took about 30 mins to do.

Overall, very very easy A. Just don't forget to attend class, as attendance a huge part of your grade. She has a tough job in teaching a 1.75 hour long class, but you can tune out and be fine, just make sure to fill out the participation. A lot of what she teaches is based off the free online textbook she provides and isn't very difficult. Exams are also online and extra credit is offered. Take her if you can!

I really liked him as a professor. It is a super easy class overall (PSYC100). Exams were completely fair and easy as long as you attended lectures and understood what he was teaching. Readings were long and to be honest, by the start of the second exam, I stopped reading them. I think Dr. Jones did a great job of explaining concepts, although, lectures were rather boring there were some interesting concepts.
There were only 2 midterms and one final, he did curve some of the midterms if the averages were lower than expected. 
Discussions were every other week for 50 mins, all you really had to do was read research papers and answer questions. That sounds like a lot of work, but it really wasn't, The TA, Michael Burrows, was really nice, and whatever you said was greeted with positive reinforcement.
Overall, the class was very easy, most likely going to end with a 97%. Would recommend

She is a great professor, very nice, laid back, makes jokes. She tries to make lecture engaging and participative. Her class is very organized and well laid out, and you know exactly when everything is due. Instructions and goals are always well laid out for you. Participation is necessary because the lecture (which is only once a week) has clicker questions. Each week there's either an (ELMs) worksheet to be done or (zoom) discussion to attend. Two midterms and a final, all of which are on ELMs. There is a research requirement, but it's not bad, just get started on it early. Overall, the class is interesting and has a very manageable courseload.

He's okay. The class is really easy but the lectures being 1 hour and 40 minutes is actually terrible. He goes off on side tangents all the time and rambles a lot. He also speaks into a microphone but he screams into it and its so loud so I always end class with a headache. He is really chill though and seems understanding and the content is so simple.
hes a nice guy but this class is too much work for a gen ed. take someone else if you can.

his class is acc kind of fun w/the right people. n you don't even have to go to the lectures half the time frfr as long as ur on campus u can log into those clicker questions n it'll let u join. the main issue lies wit the TA's since they tend to grade a bit harshly. Overall u can easily pass this class with a B+ or even an A+ if ur a tryhard. dude is super chill ! !

Take someone else if you can. He;s a nice guy and you can tell he's passionate about the material but its way too much for a gen ed. The TA's grading was very nitpicky and would lose points for the smallest things. The exams would barely have content we learned in class. The first one was so bad he had to curve it (for psyc100..). Definitely not the professor I would take if you needed to get this class out the way or need an Easy A.

Definitely an easy A. Class met once a week and discussion is online every other week. The only annoying thing is that you have to complete two in person surveys that take an hour to complete, but if you get them out of the way at the beginning then you're basically done for the semester. The discussion work was super easy. Professor is great, and I would defiantly recommend this class.

Very easy A, Although I got a B- because I would lose points on Writing Assignments(WA). Honestly, the WA SUCKS, but it wasn't very time consuming. Discussion every other week on zoom. I personally did not attend the lecture but would get the participation points since I would join the clicker. TAKE HER THIS IS EASY DSNS

After four years of various professors, I had the absolute worst experience with this professor that still negatively impacts me to this day. Without sparing personal details: He put me through extreme unnecessary stress my freshman year during the peak of COVID. Tried to "teach me lessons" the hard way which he bragged about doing to various other students. His lessons didn't help me at all throughout my four successful years - instead they remind me of a time when I wanted to drop out of college because of how terrible my experience was with him. I still tell the horror stories to family and friends as they sit in shock with how he treated me and how I accepted it as a clueless freshman. His class, however, was incredibly easy. Especially since I was an IB student who already took psychology. In all honesty, he is a fine professor, if you're lucky to never deal with him personally. I just don't think he should have the control that he does over students, because he takes advantage of it.
Really cares about students success. Best professor I've had at UMD.

Took him for PSYC100 over the summer - super chill professor and exams/quizzes are very reasonable. The exams are a bit long but very doable, the slides are basically all you need. He's pretty easy to reach out to as well. 100% recommend him for a psychology class.

WOW! This class was a breeze. Learned so much and was zero effort. Lecture attendance is required, the lecture is once a week and so is the discussion but the discussion was online. I took this class in the Spring 2024. There are worksheets and writing assignments that do not take long at all and are honestly busy work that is unnecessary but low-key. Discussion groups meet every other Friday on Zoom and since they were online it was nice because mine was at 9 am and I could do it from bed. You have to complete 5 study credits which are also so easy, 3 online and two in person. Dr. Abi is right, do these asap and keep checking the website until you have completed everything. I did mine quickly but I know people who struggled to get their credits because the studies fill up and then by the end of the semester it can take a toll on your grade which is unnecessary because I got a 104 in the class by doing mine in the first month of the semester. Exams are online and not difficult, all multiple choice, so know the information and you'll do just fine. They are long and not a lot of time which is honestly the only bad thing i can say. Syllabus quizzes were easy points and one was dropped at the end. There were also exam reflections that took 5 minutes to complete after the exam and extra credit as well which is why I ended with 104. Participation in lecture is determined by clicker questions which were also easy. you did not have to get them right and most were opinionated polls. Everything was open note and open textbook but that doesnt help you with exams because of the time limit which is understandable so you should be knowledgeable for your own sake. Overall, i took thing in Spring 2024 and it was amazing

Nicest & best professor ever!!! Genuinely cares about you and wants you to succeed. The class is easy if you keep up with the work. There are 3 exams all open note and asynchronous. If you take good notes during lectures you will be completely fine in this class. She also offers extra credit through SONA studies which are super easy. Aside from the exams there are also chapter quiz's and a couple writing assignments. Overall, I would definitely recommend this class and this professor, a great introductory class to psychology!
Super nice guy. Lectures are ok to go to. Class is not too much work, although there are three exams that cover a lot of content.

Great guy, very accommodating and class is interesting. He is very fair with grading and content, however, TAs are typically not. He often runs behind on lectures and content, but everything is available online

Dr. Jones is very nice and will help you if you need it, you can also reach out for PSYC recs and career exploration. i would keep in mind, the work load is a slightly dense with the readings and some writing assignment however i feel its manageable. TA's harsh grading is really the only downside. attending lectures benefits you as tests are based on it but they're recorded and clickers can be logged in at home for attendance so it's pretty easy to skip.

Dr. Barnet is great! The lectures were very long (1 hour 40 minutes) but he tries to make them as interesting as possible. His TAs are great! The assignments during discussion are a bit tedious, but it's easy to do well on them. The class has weekly worksheets based on the online textbook, five short-essay assignments, and three exams. For this semester, he dropped the exam with the lowest performance. There was no final. Exams are all multiple choice. They were graded an hour after being taken. He's a great guy and I highly recommend taking PSYC100 with him!

Dr. Abi is a great professor, and this is overall a very easy class, especially if you have some prior psych knowledge. There was a chapter in the free textbook each week that you had to take notes on, then she would lecture on some parts of the chapter. The lecture was pretty long and boring, but it was not bad. There was a discussion every other week and you had a few assignments each week for it, but nothing that was hard. The exams are all open note and the final is not cumulative. Overall, I would definitely recommend
Literally the best professor you can ask for. Exams are kinda hard especially if you don't study much but he drops your lowest test score and all the other coursework is so easy.

Dr. Barnet has been my favorite professor this semester. I went into PSYC100 being very nervous because I did not take AP Psych in high school and I did not know what to expect. His lectures were very interesting and I enjoyed the quick pace and his ability to interact with the class. He drops the lowest exam grade out of three exams. The exams are multiple-choice and have around 70 questions. I did very well on all of them with only a few days of studying. This class is mostly based on memorization and understanding past experiments. I recommend taking this course and potentially others!

I'm not going to lie. If you get anything below a B+, that's a YOU issue. He is a really great professor and super understanding. He is also very funny. The TAs are fair/easy graders, too for writing assignments, and his exams are easy. He recorded all his lectures and reminded you almost every Tuesday to complete your SONAs. Take him as soon as you can, Im going to take him for PYSC 200 as well.

Dr. Barnet is a very good professor. The lecture is long, but it was only once a week. The TA discussion sessions are very easy, and the assignments are all group work that you then go over as a class. Make sure to go to your discussion sections because these assignments are easy grade boosts and if you go you won't lose a point on a single one. The tests match the content learned in class and he also drops your lowest test grade of the 3. He drops a few other low grades on the easy textbook worksheets and overall it's very easy to get an A with Dr. Barnet.

Love Dr. Barnett! Chill guy that's very passionate about psychology. His lectures are long, but lowkey they go by pretty fast. He sometimes goes off topic during lectures, but it's not a big deal. We had three exams, no final, and he dropped the lowest exam score. The exams are all multiple choice. We also had weekly chapter quizzes and 5 short essay assignments, but they honestly didn't take too much time to do. Discussion assignments were a bit repetitive, but my TA was amazing and tried her best to help us get full marks on them. Dr. Barnett also dropped our lowest chapter quiz score and discussion assignment. Overall, he made psychology very interesting, and I highly recommend taking him.

Dr. Jones is a really nice professor and has engaging lectures. It's pretty interactive with polling even though it is a lecture hall. He also records every lecture so it is easy to make up. Exams were pretty straightforward as it just covered material that was covered in lectures. Homework consisted of reading checks based on the textbook and writing assignments when you don't have discussion. The reading checks were word-for-word from the textbook, but the writing assignments were sort of graded very nitpicky, but not so much that actually affected my grade in any way. Only downside to this class was that it was 1 hour and 40 mins long so my advice is to not take it at 9 am and take it later in the day.
He is so caring and understanding. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Barnet is super great! The class is very easy, I didn’t even have to take the last exam since he dropped the last one! Grading on the writing assignments was a little bit harder, but they aren’t a big percent of your grade. I’d definitely recommend him if you want a easy introduction to psych :)

Dr. Jones is just a chill guy. He's really understanding and communicates everything very well. He's open to providing resources even outside of the classroom. He's also really funny and shows that he cares for his students.

Most amazing Psychology professor at UMD. She truly cares about her students and literally all of her exams are online and open notes, making it low stress. She offered extra credit via clickers and it was a really interactive class. This has been one of my favorite classes I have taken at UMD. 100/10

Really good professor! He records all his lectures so you can watch later, but make sure you actually watch them if you don’t attend lectures because that’s what all of his exams are about. Only downside to this course is the reading checks which really just prepare you for what the next lecture is about, but can be lengthy and aren’t on exams, but it’s still easy to complete. He also makes jokes during lectures and is really funny! Definitely would recommend him, he made me excited to come to a 9am class.

I love Dr. Barnet! He is an amazing teacher and literally tells you during lecture what is going to be on the exam. The class is really easy and he drops one of the exams so I didn't even have to take the last one. There wasn't even a final for the class so that was really nice. He's a super nice guy and welcomes people to office hours if you have questions. There are around 5 writing assignments, but they aren't very hard if you look at what the rubric is expecting. There are a lot of discussions activities too but they usually aren't too hard since you only focus on one portion of it in a small group. Pretty easy gen ed if that's what you are looking for. I recommend Dr. Barnet!!

Dr. Jones is a great professor. He made all the exams non-cumulative and for the final he gave us the opportunity to take it online because he wanted to be considerate of people who had to travel back home. Ultimately, an amazing professor and I'd highly recommend him.

If you need an easy DSNS, this class is for you. Literally, everything was a cakewalk. The only annoying thing I would say is the clicker questions that you have to pay for a subscription to do. You also have to show up to a useless discussion every other week, but participation should be given to you just for showing up and saying a word or two. I highly recommend this class, It's dumb easy, and chill, cool professor too.

Really really kind! Responds to emails quickly. Tests are take home, unlimited time and open note. She’s very easy to communicate with. She begins each class with reviewing upcoming work with is super helpful. She gives you all the tools to succeed-Take this class!

I loved Dr. Abi! I am very much not a STEM student, but she made lectures very engaging all semester, with a lot of real world examples and student-professor interaction to keep things interesting. She was also very approachable with questions both in person and via email. I would very much recommend her for this course, especially if you're inexperienced in psychology like I am.

Fantastic professor would absolutely recommend him! Even though this class was online (Winter session), his swagger, kindness, availability, understanding, passion, and care all shone through nonetheless.

Professor Parham is the best remote professor I have ever had. He is very understanding if you need to turn things in later or if you need to question a grade. Overall the class was super easy especially for the amount of time a winter class is.

Easy class but I have found that in a lot of easier classes, professors actively find points to take off which I don't appreciate, and that is exactly what she does. She is not open to grade changes at all, even with confusing exam questions or Canvas technicalities. So it was ok but not my favorite class.
Goat, easy exams and easy class, attendance not mandatory. LOVE HIM

Amazing Professor who is very passionate and cares alot of psychology in general. Easy class consists of three exams (drops one) so if you do well on the first two you do not need to take the last one. Writing assignments which take no more than 40 minutes, discussion online which is very easy all you have to do is show up and complete a group worksheet. You can leave after like 15-20 minutes in discussion. The exams are multiple choice 50-60 questions for each exam. Very easy if you study a couple hours a few days before the exam.

He is amazing!! He is so attentive to his students, so much so that he made our final exam online AND open note. His lectures are soooo long (1hr and 40mins) and he goes to the very last minute every time but they are interesting. I’m lucky I took this class in high school though or else I would not be able to absorb so much information in that time. His exams are super easy and straightforward, no trick questions whatsoever. Our class got an average of 86 or something on an exam he thought was hard. He’s also very passionate about the content and wants everyone to love psych as much as he does. Very great professor, definitely take him if you think you can make it through an almost 2 hour lecture once a week.

WHAT AN EASY CLASS FR. LIKEEE TAKE HERRR. On top of being such a sweet heart (though never got close to her) she is genuine like u can literally see her and see how she cares like truly. Super easy class, super easy A. Ima break this down for you. There are worksheets which are based on the reading but are super easy, writing assignments which are due when you have your discussion. Literally, one week you gonna have discussion, one week not, depending on what group you are, so if youre group A, your group will have discussion first and then a writing assignment. The other group (B) doesn't have discussion but they are a discussion post. So on. 2 midterms. Both OPEN NOTE!!! Yup, yall read that right... ONLINE TOO, you have from like 3 - 6 to do the exam (which takes like 60 minutres) but you have like 3 hours fr, as long as u complete it within that time frame. FINAL EXAM ONLINE TOO. Thats it

I like this Professor. He’s a great guy who helps us with the classes and records every lectures. He likes to tell jokes during class to entertain the class. His exams are cumulative and the final is online.

I like this Professor. He’s a great guy who helps us with the classes and records every lectures. He's also open to providing resources to everyone even outside of the classroom He likes to tell jokes during class to entertain the class. His exams are cumulative and the final is online.

Classes can feel long but they are only once a week. So much extra credit you don't know what to do with it. Exams are online and there are only 3. Mandatory discussion every other week and on the off week there is a worksheet which is essentially a quiz that is word for word from the textbook. I missed discussion one week and she gave me a relatively challenging make up assignment that she didn't have to give me. Take Dr. Nicolas please you will pass.

Professor Parham is the nicest, most chill, and one of the best professors at UMD. His lectures are always recorded (attendance not required), and presentations posted well before class time. There are 3 total exams: 2 midterms and the final is the exact same format as the midterms. Prof. Parham always does an exam review session before the exams where he goes over each individual question on the exam and essentially tells you the answer/what to study. 6 essays throughout the semester, with the lowest grade dropped (put in some effort for the first 5 essays, and you won't have to do the last one). Essays are set to be due at 11:59PM of the given day, however Prof. Parham does not take any points off if you submit the assignment by 10AM the following day. The textbook is free (OpenPSYC), and for each chapter of the textbook there's a quiz based on that chapter's content (open note). Prof. Parham has some learning checks/participation assignments either on Kahoot or VoiceThreads where he just wants to know that you understand the content. There are a few extra credit opportunities, mainly given at the end of the semester. If you have the chance to take a class with him, PLEASE DO, he is such a genuinely nice guy and he genuinely cares about his students' wellbeing, even though he teaches via Zoom. 

TL;DR: Prof. Parham is a kind, low-stress, and highly supportive professor who offers clear exam prep, manageable essays, and a generous grading policy. Take a class with him if you can.
Great professor and structured class. Discussions were mandatory every other week. There isn't too much work outside of class, mainly just studying for the exams.

He is a great storyteller, but an improvable professor.
My points are the same as those of the other who rate him low, you cannot expect too much exam content from class. He cannot grade your course credit counter with Syllybus, so you cannot fully trust the grading board on your dashboard, but calculate it yourself. Apart from that, the writing and discussion sessions are arranged alternately, so you need to have a discussion this week and do the writing next week. This confused me, especially in the first few weeks.
If you are a psychology-related major or confident that you will cover everything in this field, Dr. Jones will be a nice choice, as he is just as engaged as most people said when having his class. Otherwise, I will not recommend him if you have PSYC100 only as a prerequisite (like me).

Simply great.

Professor Parham feels just so chill, as many reviews below me say. It's fully online, videos recorded, and work consists of pretty easy assignments: 3 online tests, online quizzes with 2 retakes, occasional Kahoot and VoiceThreads, etc. The essays are the only somewhat tricky parts, as you can lose points, but you get one dropped at the end, so it's usually nice. 

Professor Parham teaches exceptionally well, and makes an interesting subject... more interesting, I guess lol. It's a class where, I know I don't need to pay attention, but sometimes I find myself tuning in just because I'm interested (and you should too!). He clearly cares about us using what we learn in our own lives, and that's overall something I enjoy about this class.

The only thing I could really critique is the fact that some tests are written weirdly from time to time, but everything else is kind of just phenomenal. If you can, this is one of the best teachers you can take at UMD.

It's a class that definitely makes me think about it a lot outside of the classroom. Benjamin actively tries to get student's attention, passionate for the field, tries to remember people's names if you're sitting up front. Three non-cumulative exams and the writing assignments can be a bit tight sometimes (and TAs are extremely strict on late assignments), overall did largely enjoy and would recommend whether taking PSYC100 as a prereq or for the major.

I didn't go to lecture so often, but he's one of the best professors I've had so far at UMD. His classes are an hour and forty minutes, which he said he could do nothing about, but he did his best to make it interesting and always gave us breaks or let us out early. There are three tests (lowest grade dropped!!!), all of which are pretty easy. Four writing assignments, also super easy. The homework is light; one assignment per week, all ChatGPTable. As are discussion worksheets, which are based on completion. His third test was online too, which was unreal. Nothing negative to say. If you're looking for an easy life science credit, or are interested in psych, take Barnet!

His class had its interesting moments but, I honestly did not care for psychology...I don't remember why I did not end up with an A, but I remember being very close to it and he did not want to round me up a decimal for whatever reason. What I do remember is his TA's grading us harshly. I wouldve taken someone else if I could in retrospect. It just felt like too much work for a gen Ed and it honestly went in my back burner a couple times. I was taking other stem courses I cared more about. Mid professor but personable guy I guess.
geniunely so easy like SO easy. So much extra credit too that its like hard no to get an A

Dr. Jones loves his job, he loves psychology, and he loves teaching. He tries to make lecture entertaining and at times involves the class in different activities that help us understand the material better. His tests were fairly easy, but he provided little to no practice tests or word banks about the topics that were going to be on the test, so you just had to learn everything and create your own practice questions, which worked in a way. Overall, I definitely recommend him for PSYC100.

Dr. Jones' classes were always engaging and I was motivated to attend every lecture even though he doesn't take attendance. He is clearly passionate about psychology and encouraged us to come talk more in-depth about it with him if we were interested. His tests were a little bit difficult to study for since we didn't get a study guide, but if you take notes in class and go over all the slideshows (including examples he discussed in class) you will do well. 
Since the class was so big we had discussion sections every other week and a writing assignment every other week. The discussions were interesting but the writing assignments felt like busy work (mostly practicing APA format). But overall, I thought this class was fun and pretty easy.

Great course to take during the summer! The course is 6 weeks during the summer, completely online with optional lectures (best if you attend the lectures), 3 exams, 12 online quizzes with retakes, 5 papers and an extra credit paper, and 5 VoiceThread recordings. One of your quizzes and papers gets dropped, so that is helpful. Exams are a mixture of the lectures, the textbook, and the worksheets. Nothing out of the ordinary will come up on an exam. Overall would recommend this course and this professor. 10/10 would take again.

A great lecturer and very knowledgeable in his teaching, his exams were pretty chilled if you study and attend the discussion sessions, and he drops the lowest exam grade. Would definitely recommend him if you need to take the class.

SO engaging and chill. Her lectures are passionate and lowkey funny sometimes, but she's also clearly very knowledgeable. This is a super good gen ed because all the tests are open note and taken at home. The notes/work can be lengthy, but never felt impossible or unreasonable.

Awesome and very relatable guy! Still remembered me even a few semesters after I took his class. Very fair exams and assignments, absolutely no complaints about this course at all. Definitely recommend him as a professor if you want to learn the material and enjoy the class.

Such an amazing class. Definitely lecture-heavy, but if you go to class, the exams are so easy. He is so reasonable, and the lectures are engaging and funny. He gives random extra credit points for answering his questions and will give you free points on exams. Talks about his kids a lot and relates them to the topics, adorable. Definitely recommend him.
He's very nice, a lot of fun, and the only reason that the 100 minute lecture is bearable. He's also totally on your side and will give you the right answer in a test if you ask him for help!

He is a great teacher, makes the content very understandable. You might have to learn some of the content outside of class because the class is only once a week. He is very sweet and funny, and the tests are pretty straightforward. I would recommend this class.

Very nice and amazing professor. The work in this class is insane though. Tons of busy work but its worth for the gen ed and easy A. I took this class for a DSNS credit and it wasn't that bad. Take this class if you are trying to get rid of a DSNS!

Dr. Jones himself is a pretty laid back guy, and his lectures are pretty interesting. The class just meets once a week and is recorded so it's a very light commitment class as long as you show up to the bi-weekly in person discussion.

The exams were (very) easy in my opinion, all multiple choice and you just need to review the content for a bit and make sure you understand it. The content is not difficult—I barely reviewed and would get over 100% on the exams (he also had extra credit). 

The only issue I had was that the discussion work is just busywork, and can be unnecessarily tedious. The grading is also not super lenient for these. If you have the choice to take a different well-rated PSYC100 professor, I would, but he's a solid choice still.

Took PSYC100 with him and he posted slides, recorded lectures, and had office hours. Responded to emails in a moderate amount of time and was friendly. Lectures a bit boring, but that sometimes comes with the nature of big lectures like this one. Some questions on exam were a bit too detailed but he always too feedback. If you put in the work to study and complete assignments on time, you'll score high in the class. Overall, I would take this class if I was freshman all over again.

Amazing professor. He's very engaging, explains things thoroughly (and makes clear when things are on the exam or not), and exams are easy (and multiple-choice). The class itself was also a lot of fun, especially his personal anecdotes and slides. For sure, take this professor.

EASIEST CLASS EVER!! This is by far one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. Discussions are once every other week and midterms/final are online. On weeks you have discussions you have a discussion post due before 9am that Friday. The weeks you don't have discussion, you have a writing assignment and worksheet due Friday 11:59pm. They're all pretty easy assignment and aren't graded harshly. SONA credits aren't hard but could be annoying if your lazy. Dr Nicloas has plenty of extra credit opportunities for this class so if you don't get at least an "A" thats on you, not her. Even if you don't need a DSNS credit I'd still take it for an elective!

Dr. Jones is one of the most engaging lecturers I've had here at UMD. I always wanted to come to class because his energy and excitement was contagious. The only gripe I have with the class is the exams, as I felt they would get extremely specific while sacrificing questions about larger, more important concepts. But, you can't change everything. The discussions were interesting, the writing exercises enhanced my understanding of vocabulary that would end up on exams, and the 9 a.m. start time didn't feel too bad. Secrets to success? Study the slides, and study EVERYTHING on them, even the studies that seem like they'd never show up on a test, because they will. Additionally, come to lecture. He records every lecture and uploads slides, but being there allows you to learn better. Would totally recommend.

Probably my favorite professor this semester, I would recommend him to anyone! His class is online and attendance is not graded, but I love the way he teaches content. He genuinely cares about all of his students and is incredibly lenient. I took PSYC100 as a GenEd and his lectures were genuinely interesting!! Please take him if you have the chance, this was a great class!
TAKE HIM!!!! He applies real life to his class, engaging, funny, smart, really loves this and wants us all to learn!

Great professor, makes the nearly two hour long lecture entertaining and engaging. Only issue is the online textbook used in the class isn't really organized, just a bunch of scientific articles and videos, and has a lot of filler content that he isn't clear on whether it will be on the test or not. Also, he doesn't really provide a ton of resources to prepare for the exams, only like five or so practice questions. Otherwise he is very kind and understanding

Definitely recommend! Tests are extremely simple if you study the vocabulary words on the slides, which are all posted. Dr. Jones is extremely passionate about the subject and wants his students to succeed.  He tries hard to make the lectures engaging, but the discussions are kinda boring and give busy work assignments. But discussions are only once every other week (depending on your section), and in the other weeks, you have an asynchronous assignment. Overall, definitely recommend!
one of the most chill and kind professors i've ever had! so many extra credit opportunities that its easy to pass with over 100%.

The class is pretty easy, and he tells you what you need to know for the exam. The readings and lectures are VERY important and will show up on the exam. He does talk about about his real life to correlate them to the stuff in class sometimes and runs over time because of it but its not crazy bad just like a few minutes here and there. He gives freebies on the tests. The lectures and class are very straight forward if you fail this class especially with him as a professor, its your fault because he gives you everything you need to pass.
Very entertaining and makes lecture fun would 100% recommend for psyc100
my goat fr. he's fun and engaging and manages to make the lectures not miserable.

hes very nice, a lot of fun, and the only reason that the long minute lecture is bearable. hes also totally on your side and will give you the right answer in a test if you ask him for help, and is also very accommodating on assignments. strongly recommend, he has horrible dad jokes :)
SUPER nice professor. All exams were open note, easy work, funny professor, 100% would recommend.

Engaging class, Professor Jones cares about the topic very deeply and keeps the lectures entertaining. Tests are very straightforward and focus directly on what you learned in class or on the once-a-week homework assignment. Discussions are very interesting with though provoking topics.

Fire teacher and has a lot of energy and passion for the topic. A lot of the lecture content is the same as slides and every lecture (minus a guest lecture) was posted on Panopto. No clickers this semester so attendance is not required except for discussion. Love that discussion is asynchronous every other week but all the assignments are busy work but require little effort. Exams are fine you just have to review more than you think and a lot of it is logic based/examples used from lectures. Take this guy for your psyc100 requirement.

This class is very easy. The professor holds one weekly lecture that’s about two hours long. All of the exams are online and closely reflect the lecture slides. Discussion is also very relaxed, and most of the time you’re let out early. The only thing I really disliked about this class was the SONA research credit requirement. It honestly felt like I was being forced to act as a research test subject just to earn an A.
