Aside from the SONA component, everything else in the course is extremely manageable, and you lowkey don’t even need to pay close attention in lecture to do well. I ended the class with like a 105% with minimal work.

Jones is a pretty good lecturer but the class can be really boring sometimes. Since it was so early I stopped going halfway through and just reviewed the lecture slides which he posts on ELMS. I would recommend doing that since sitting through 100 minutes can be a lot. There is also a lot of busy work but it was all really easy. The exams (2 midterms and a non cumulative final) were in person this year and they were all multichoice. Jones did add a 1% curve on everyone's final grade, meaning an 89.00% would be an A-. I'd say take him if you need the NS gen ed or if your major requires PSYC100.

Dr. Abi's lectures were very engaging and understandable. She clearly cared for the well-being of each student and was very open and friendly. She welcomed questions and enjoyed teaching about psychology. Her class did require us to buy PointSolutions for in-class clicker questions that were graded on participation. I felt that these clicker questions were unnecessary and a waste of money, especially since she also directed questions toward the class and expected students to raise their hands to answer. The clicker questions didn't really help my understanding of the content either and seemed to be mainly for engagement purposes. Lectures were recorded, and the textbook was free.

Grades were not curved and used around the standard grade cutoffs. Grades consisted of 3 exams, 5 worksheets, 3 syllabus quizzes, 5 discussions, 4 writing assignments, 2 exam reflections, clickers, and 5 SONA research credits. All exams were online, open-note, take-home, and multiple-choice. They covered lecture content, textbook content, and discussion content, but since they were open-note, you could easily get 100% using ctrl+F. Each week, we switched off between either attending discussion or completing a worksheet and writing assignment. These were all easy A's as long as you followed the rubric and instructions. All the other assignments were also really easy, but I'd recommend getting the SONA credits done early to avoid forgetting about them. There were also a lot of easy extra credit opportunities that boosted your grade.

Overall, this was a very laid-back class with a low time commitment, but you still learn a lot about the basics of psychology.

Overall great professor and great class. He teaches you how to study for exams and what specific content/sections will be covered. Exams consisted of multiple choice questions, including knowledge from what was mentioned in class (definitely take notes) and some of what is covered in the online text. Dr. Botanov was very engaging and interactive with students during class, which helped keep everyone interested and actually comprehend what was being taught. You can tell he truly wants everyone to succeed and get a good grade. Definitely recommend taking this professor!

Dr. Jones is super chill and his lectures are nice. I never attended class (cuz it was really long and attendance isn't mandatory) but his lecture recordings were always posted and watching them is super helpful especially for exams. Speaking of exams they're usually 30-40 multiple choice questions and almost everything is either from the lectures, power points, and textbooks. As for assignments it was just weekly readings and quizzes that followed them or short papers. The one thing I'd say I didn't like was discussions, they're TA run and my TA was super mean and always angry during class and it just killed the vibe. Overall, the class is interesting I learned a lot of new things.
Great Professor! Records lectures and is very approachable. Class doesn’t require too much time, but you do have to stay on top of your work. Exams are very straightforward if you look over lectures!

PSYC100 with Dr. Jones was great. He's super chill and lectures are pretty straightforward. Exams were fairly straightforward, with multiple choice applications-based questions. As long as you pay attention in class and study the slides, you'll be fine. Weekly discussions are kind of boring, but depending on your TA you'll usually get out early anyways. Minimal out of class assignments (weekly readings/reading check quizzes, and short writing assignments scattered throughout). Overall, a super interesting class. Highly recommend.

I took his class over winter break and was worried it would take up a lot of my time but it truly didn't. I have taken psych courses in the past so I did have less to learn, but the PPTs and the lecture videos didn't take too much time and the assignments were really quick and easy. Such a good class to take over a break. He is also a really nice guy and seems to really care about his students. The TAs were also really nice and helpful when you email them. I really enjoyed this class and almost wish I would have taken his class in person.

He is such an amazing person and teacher. I am a sophomore and have yet to have a professor here that I actually liked, but he was genuinely awesome and seems to really care about what he is teaching and his students. Definitely recommend taking a class with him if you can.

Dr. Jones is such a nice teacher! He tried to make his lectures as engaging as possible, and he always posted recordings and announcements. My TA was super nice for discussion and those assignments were always chill. The exams were a little difficult, but they are only hard if you study only a week before or if you overthink your answers. Otherwise, he’s a very understanding teacher and the class was very chill. Highly recommend!

Great teacher, happy guy who is excited to teach and wants to engage the class. I think there were 2 midterms and the final was not cumulative. Just review the slides (which he posts) and the textbook (free, online) and you'll do good on exams. I would 100% take his class again, he's gonna be a great dad for his kid coming soon!

Even though Dr. Jones is a bit of a rambler, his tangents are so funny and he genuinely made this class interesting. Overall, the class is not at all difficult. Reading checks are open note, he records his lectures in their entirety, and a decent portion of your grade is from SONA psychology study participation! Loved this class and the contents!

To succeed, genuinely just go to lectures, pay attention, and take notes. If you're too lazy for that, though, you could lowkey marathon watch them the day before and still probably get the grade! Also go to discussions every other week, they are mandatory! The topics in them are often pretty interesting anyways :) 

Great class!

One of the BEST professor out there. Professor Botanov makes the class engaging and entertaining, even though it is almost a two hour class. The discussions online are amazing and super easy and understandable. All you have to do to get a good grade in this class is do the work on time and show up. There are times when he will discuss something in class more in depth than what show in readings or on the slides, and most of the time these concepts show up on the exam. The exams are straight forward (not trying to trick you) and as long as you do the section reviews and go to class, you will at least get a B-. Lastly, for anyone taking the class, make sure you do the SONA early. There are way more options and easier options than waiting until the last couple weeks of the semester.

As someone who had no prior experience with psychology, Dr. Jones was great at introducing the subject material. He really cares about the success of his students, and the workload was extremely manageable. Exams were very easy if you read the book and paid attention to the lecture slides, both of which he provided online. Very accessible outside of class during office hours and by email, so reach out if you have any questions.

Super easy class. Would definitely recommend. Dr. Jones is very nice and structures the course so it is almost impossible to fail the class if you just review the lecture slides. Although the lecture is long, it doesn't feel like it's being dragged out and I enjoyed his teaching.

Literally don’t take this professor. There are so many other professors who make/teach psyc100 so much easier. We only have one two hour lecture per week which makes it really hard for dr. botanov to squeeze in as much information as possible, which we supplement by reading the textbook, but the textbook is so extensive you had no idea what he really wants. He drones on a lot during lecture, which may be engaging for some people, but  it’s really annoying when it’s the only lecture of the week and we have so much information to cover. Our class average for the first exam was around a 60, which is kinda sad considering this is psyc100 and half the professors who teach this class make exams open note and online. take someone else. i’m warning you.

name: PSYC100
title: Introduction to Psychology
description: A basic introductory course intended to bring the student into contact with the major problems confronting psychology and the more important attempts at their solution. Discussion sections do not meet until after first lecture. Research requirement: may involve participation in research. Click here for course syllabus.
